title.zh: 卷二百八十四 列傳第一百七十二 儒林三
title.raw: 卷二百八十四 列傳第一百七十二 儒林三 Volume 284 Biographies 172: Confucian Scholars 3

sentences.zh: 孔希學

translations.literal: Kong Xixue
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xixue

sentences.zh: （孔彥繩）〉

translations.literal: (Kong Yansheng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Kong Yansheng)]〉

sentences.zh: 顏希惠曾質粹孔聞禮孟希文仲於陛周冕程接道程克仁張文運邵繼祖朱梴朱墅

translations.literal: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, Zhu Shu
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, and Zhu Shu

sentences.zh: 孔希學，字士行，先聖五十六代孫也，世居曲阜。

translations.literal: Kong Xixue, courtesy name Shixing, was a descendant of the Sage in the fifty-sixth generation, and his clan had long lived in Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xixue, whose courtesy name was Shixing, was a fifty-sixth-generation descendant of the Sage; his family had lived in Qufu for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖思晦，字明道，仕元為教諭，有學行。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sihui, courtesy name Mingdao, served the Yuan as an instructor and had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sihui, styled Mingdao, held an instructorship under the Yuan and was known for scholarship and integrity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，以思晦襲封衍聖公，卒謚文肅，子克堅襲。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Renzong, Sihui inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Yan Sheng; on his death he was posthumously titled Wensu, and his son Kejian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong of Yuan, Sihui inherited the title Duke of Yan Sheng; when he died he was given the posthumous name Wensu, and his son Kejian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 克堅，字璟夫。

translations.literal: Kejian, courtesy name Jingfu.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian, whose courtesy name was Jingfu.

sentences.zh: 至正六年，中書言衍聖公階止嘉議大夫，與爵不稱，乃進通奉大夫，予銀印。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng, the Secretariat said the Duke of Yan Sheng's rank stopped at Grand Master for Aspiration with Purpose, which did not match his title, so he was promoted to Grand Master for Imperial Audience and given a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhizheng, the Secretariat reported that the Duke of Yan Sheng's rank had been only Grand Master for Aspiration with Purpose—ill-matched to his title—so he was raised to Grand Master for Imperial Audience and granted a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 十五年有薦其明習禮樂者，征為同知太常禮儀院事，以子希學襲封。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year someone recommended him as well versed in ritual and music; he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and his son Xixue inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recommended as thoroughly versed in ritual and music, summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and replaced in the hereditary title by his son Xixue.

sentences.zh: 克堅累遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Kejian was promoted in succession to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian rose in due course to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，克堅謝病還闕里，後起集賢學士、山東廉訪使，皆不赴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Kejian resigned on grounds of illness and returned to Que li; later he was recalled as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and as Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong, but he went to neither post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Kejian pleaded illness and went home to Qufu; later appointments as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong he likewise declined.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年三月，徐達下濟寧，克堅稱疾，遣希學來見，達送之京師。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Hongwu, Xu Da took Jining; Kejian claimed illness and sent Xixue to present himself; Da escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Hongwu 1, when Xu Da captured Jining, Kejian pleaded illness and sent Xixue to pay his respects; Xu Da had him escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 希學奏父病不能行，太祖敕諭克堅，末言「稱疾則不可」。

translations.literal: Xixue reported that his father was ill and could not travel; the Taizu issued an edict to Kejian, ending with the words "to claim illness will not do."
translations.idiomatic: Xixue explained that his father was too ill to travel; the founding emperor sent Kejian an edict that closed with the warning, "Pleading illness will not be accepted."

sentences.zh: 會克堅亦來朝，遇使者淮安，惶恐兼程進，見於謹身殿問以年，對曰：「臣年五十有三。

translations.literal: As it happened Kejian also came to court; he met the envoy at Huai'an, and in alarm hurried on by forced stages; he was received at the Hall of Self-Discipline and asked his age; he replied, "Your subject is fifty-three."
translations.idiomatic: Kejian came to court after all, met the imperial messenger at Huai'an, and in alarm pressed on night and day; received in the Hall of Self-Discipline, he was asked his age and answered, "Your subject is fifty-three."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「爾年未邁，而病嬰之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your years have not yet reached the threshold, yet illness afflicts you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are not yet old, yet you are stricken with illness."

sentences.zh: 今不煩爾以官。

translations.literal: For now I will not trouble you with office.
translations.idiomatic: For the present I will not burden you with office.

sentences.zh: 爾家，先聖後，子孫不可不學。

translations.literal: Your house is descended from the Sage; the descendants must not fail to study.
translations.idiomatic: Your family springs from the Sage; its descendants must not neglect learning.

sentences.zh: 爾子溫厚，俾進學。

translations.literal: Your son is gentle and substantial; have him advance in study.
translations.idiomatic: Your son is mild and steady—see that he pursues his studies.

sentences.zh: 」克堅頓首謝。

translations.literal: Kejian bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 即日賜宅一區，馬一匹，米二十石。

translations.literal: That same day he was granted one residence, one horse, and twenty piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he received a residence, a horse, and twenty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 明日復召見，命以訓厲族人。

translations.literal: The next day he was summoned again and ordered to admonish and encourage his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was summoned again and charged to instruct and discipline his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 因顧侍臣曰：「先聖後，特優禮之，養以祿而不任以事也。」

translations.literal: Turning to the attending ministers he said, "Descendants of the Sage are specially favored: they are maintained with stipends but not charged with duties."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants he said, "Descendants of the Sage receive exceptional honor—they are kept on stipends but not assigned to office."

sentences.zh: 十一月命希學襲封衍聖公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xixue was ordered to inherit the enfeoffment as Duke of Yan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xixue was commanded to inherit the title Duke of Yan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 置官屬，曰掌書，曰典籍，曰司樂，曰知印，曰奏差，曰書寫，各一人。

translations.literal: Staff offices were established: Director of Documents, Director of the Canon, Director of Music, Keeper of the Seal, Memorial Courier, and Scribe—one man for each.
translations.idiomatic: A staff was appointed—Director of Documents, Director of the Canon, Director of Music, Keeper of the Seal, Memorial Courier, and Scribe—one holder for each post.

sentences.zh: 立孔、顏、孟三氏教授司，教授、學錄、學司各一人。

translations.literal: An Instructional Office for the three clans of Kong, Yan, and Meng was established, with one Instructor, one Recorder, and one Registrar each.
translations.idiomatic: An instructional office for the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans was set up, each with one professor, one recorder, and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 立尼山、洙泗二書院，各設山長一人。

translations.literal: The Ni Mountain and Zhu-Si Academies were established, each with one mountain chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Ni Mountain and Zhu-Si academies were founded, each headed by a mountain chief.

sentences.zh: 復孔氏子孫及顏、孟大宗子孫徭役。

translations.literal: Corvée labor was restored for descendants of the Kong clan and for descendants of the main lines of Yan and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée obligations were lifted for Kong descendants and for heirs of the main Yan and Meng lines.

sentences.zh: 又命其族人希大為曲阜世襲知縣。

translations.literal: His clansman Xida was also appointed hereditary magistrate of Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Xida was also made hereditary magistrate of Qufu.

sentences.zh: 而進衍聖公秩二品，階資善大夫。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yan Sheng was advanced to the second rank, with the grade of Grand Master for Fostering Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yan Sheng was raised to second rank, with the grade Grand Master for Fostering Goodness.

sentences.zh: 賜之誥曰：「古之聖人，自羲、農至於文、武，法天治民，明並日月，德化之盛莫有加焉。

translations.literal: An investiture patent was granted, saying: "The sages of antiquity, from Fu Xi and Shen Nong down to King Wen and King Wu, took Heaven as their model in governing the people; their brilliance matched sun and moon, and the fullness of their virtue and transformation had no superior."
translations.idiomatic: He was given an investiture patent that read: "The sages of old—from Fu Xi and Shen Nong to King Wen and King Wu—governed the people on Heaven's pattern; their brilliance rivaled the sun and moon, and none surpassed the reach of their virtue and transforming power."

sentences.zh: 然皆隨時制宜，世有因革。

translations.literal: Yet each adapted measures to the times, and ages had their inheritances and reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each adapted policy to the age, and every era brought its own inheritances and reforms.

sentences.zh: 至於孔子，雖不得其位，會前聖之道而通之，以垂教萬世，為帝者師。

translations.literal: As for Confucius, though he did not obtain the throne, he gathered the Way of the former sages and made it one, to hand down teaching for ten thousand generations, becoming teacher to emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, though he never held supreme power, united the Way of the sages who came before him and handed it down for all ages—teacher to every ruler.

sentences.zh: 其孫子思，又能傳述而名言之，以極其盛。

translations.literal: His grandson Zisi could also transmit and set it forth in words, bringing it to its fullness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zisi in turn transmitted and articulated that teaching until it reached its full height.

sentences.zh: 有國家者，求其統緒，尊其爵號，蓋所以崇德報功也。

translations.literal: Those who possess a state seek their line of descent and honor their titles and ranks—this is how virtue is exalted and merit requited.
translations.idiomatic: Every state seeks out their line of descent and honors their titles—how else to exalt virtue and repay merit?

sentences.zh: 歷代以來，膺襲封者或不能繩其祖武，朕甚閔焉。

translations.literal: Through successive dynasties those who inherited the enfeoffment could not always continue their ancestors' achievements, and We are deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Down the ages, not every heir to the title has matched his forebears' achievement, and this grieves Us deeply.

sentences.zh: 當臨馭之初，訪世襲者得五十六代孫孔希學，大宗是紹，爰行典禮，以致褒崇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Our rule We sought the hereditary heir and found the fifty-sixth-generation descendant Kong Xixue; the main line was continued, and We thereupon carried out the canonical rites to extend praise and honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Our reign We sought the hereditary heir and found Kong Xixue, fifty-sixth in descent; with the main line thus secured, We performed the canonical rites of praise and honor.

sentences.zh: 爾其領袖世儒，益展聖道之用於當世，以副朕之至望，豈不偉歟！

translations.literal: You shall lead the scholars of the age, further unfold the Sage's Way for use in the present world, to fulfill Our utmost expectation—how is this not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Lead the scholars of your generation; bring the Sage's Way fully to bear on the present age, and fulfill Our highest hopes—what achievement could be greater?

sentences.zh: 」希大階承事郎，賜之敕。

translations.literal: Xida was given the grade of Attendant Gentleman and granted an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xida received the grade Attendant Gentleman and was granted an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 三年春，克堅以疾告歸，遣中使慰問。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Kejian asked leave to return on grounds of illness; palace envoys were sent to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Kejian petitioned to go home on account of illness, and palace envoys were dispatched to console him.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，詔給驛還家，賜白金文綺，舟次邳州卒。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, an edict granted relay transport for his return home and bestowed white gold and patterned silks; he died when his boat reached Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, an edict provided relay horses for the journey home and granted white gold and brocade; he died when his boat reached Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，希學服闋入朝，命所司致廩餼，從人皆有賜，復勞以敕，賜襲衣冠帶。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, when mourning was ended, Xixue entered court; the responsible offices were ordered to provide grain and meat, all attendants received gifts, and he was again comforted by edict and granted the robes, cap, and belt of inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year Xixue came to court after mourning; the authorities were told to supply his provisions, every attendant was rewarded, he was again honored by edict, and received the ceremonial robes, cap, and belt of his title.

sentences.zh: 九月辭歸，命翰林官餞於光祿寺，賚白金文綺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he took leave to return; Hanlin officials were ordered to give a farewell feast at the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and white gold and patterned silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he took his leave; Hanlin scholars were ordered to host a farewell feast at the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and he was given white gold and brocade.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，希學言：「先聖廟堂廊廡圮壞，祭器、樂器、法服不備，乞命有司修治。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Xixue said: "The halls and corridors of the Sage's temple are collapsed and ruined; sacrificial vessels, musical instruments, and ritual garments are not complete—we beg that the responsible offices be ordered to repair them."
translations.idiomatic: The following second month Xixue reported: "The Sage's temple halls and cloisters are in ruins; sacrificial vessels, musical instruments, and ritual vestments are incomplete—we ask that the proper offices be charged with repairs."

sentences.zh: 先世田，兵後多蕪，而征賦如故，乞減免。

translations.literal: The fields of former generations, after the wars, are largely waste, yet levies remain as before—we beg reduction and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestral fields lie largely fallow after the wars, yet taxes are levied as before—we beg for relief and exemption.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: Both requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 自是，每歲入朝，班亞丞相，皆加宴賚。

translations.literal: From then on, each year when he came to court he ranked next below the chief minister, and banquets and gifts were always added.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on his annual visits to court he took rank just below the chief minister and always received banquets and gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 希學好讀書，善隸法，文詞爾雅。

translations.literal: Xixue loved reading, was skilled in clerical script, and his literary phrasing was refined.
translations.idiomatic: Xixue was a devoted reader, wrote excellent clerical script, and composed in an elegant style.

sentences.zh: 每賓客宴集，談笑揮灑，爛然成章。

translations.literal: Whenever guests gathered for feasts, in talk and laughter he would pour forth words that formed brilliant compositions.
translations.idiomatic: At every gathering of guests his conversation flowed freely, turning talk and laughter into polished prose.

sentences.zh: 承大亂之後，廟貌服物，畢力修舉，盡還舊觀。

translations.literal: After the great disorder, he devoted his full strength to restoring the temple's appearance and ritual objects, returning everything to its former aspect.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of the great upheaval he threw all his energy into restoring the temple precinct and its ritual furnishings until the old splendor was fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 命守臣致祭。

translations.literal: The local guardian officials were ordered to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials were ordered to conduct the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 子訥，字言伯，十七年正月襲封。

translations.literal: His son Ne, courtesy name Yanbo, inherited the enfeoffment in the first month of the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ne, styled Yanbo, inherited the title in the first month of the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 命禮官以教坊樂導送至國學，學官率諸生二千餘人迎於成賢街。

translations.literal: Ritual officials were ordered to escort him with music from the Music Office to the Imperial Academy; the academy officers led more than two thousand students to welcome him at Chengxian Street.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials were told to escort him with Music Office ensembles to the Imperial Academy, where the officers led more than two thousand students to welcome him on Chengxian Street.

sentences.zh: 自後，每歲入覲，給符乘傳。

translations.literal: Afterward, each year when he came to audience, tally and relay transport were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he received travel tallies and relay horses for his annual audiences at court.

sentences.zh: 帝既革丞相官，遂令班文臣首。

translations.literal: After the emperor abolished the office of chief minister, he was ordered to rank first among civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor abolished the chief ministership, Ne was placed at the head of the civil roster.

sentences.zh: 訥性恭謹，處宗黨有恩。

translations.literal: Ne's nature was respectful and careful; in dealing with his clan he showed kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was respectful and careful by nature and treated his clansmen with generosity.

sentences.zh: 建文二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jianwen 2.

sentences.zh: 子公鑒襲。

translations.literal: His son Gongjian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongjian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 公鑒，字昭文，有孝行，嗣爵二年卒。

translations.literal: Gongjian, courtesy name Zhaowen, had filial conduct; he died two years after inheriting the title.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjian, styled Zhaowen, was known for filial piety and died two years after succeeding to the title.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，遣使致祭。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu took the throne, envoys were sent to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor came to the throne, envoys were dispatched to conduct the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 子彥縉，字朝紳，永樂八年襲，甫十歲，命肄業國學，久之遺歸。

translations.literal: His son Yanshen, courtesy name Chaoshen, inherited in the eighth year of Yongle; he was only ten, and was ordered to pursue studies at the Imperial Academy; after a long while he was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanshen, styled Chaoshen, inherited in Yongle 8 at the age of ten; he was sent to study at the Imperial Academy and, after a long stay, allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 十五年修闕里文廟成，禦制碑文勒石。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the repair of the Confucian temple at Que li was completed, and an imperially composed inscription was carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the restoration of the Qufu temple was finished, and the emperor's own inscription was cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 仁宗踐阼，彥縉來朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, Yanshen came to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor took the throne, Yanshen came to court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗語侍臣曰：「外蕃貢使皆有公館。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said to his attending ministers: "Tributary envoys from foreign lands all have official lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong emperor told his attendants: "Foreign tributary envoys all have official lodges.

sentences.zh: 衍聖公假館民間，非崇儒重道意。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yan Sheng lodges among the common people—this is not the intent of honoring Confucian learning and revering the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yan Sheng lodges in private homes—that is hardly how We honor Confucian learning and the Way.

sentences.zh: 」遂賜宅東安門外。

translations.literal: A residence outside the Dong'an Gate was thereupon granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a residence outside the Dong'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年，彥縉將遣使福建市書，咨禮部，部臣以聞，命市與之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande, Yanshen was about to send an envoy to Fujian to purchase books; he consulted the Ministry of Rites, and the ministry officials reported upward; he was ordered to have the books purchased for him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 Yanshen planned to send an agent to Fujian to buy books; he consulted the Ministry of Rites, the matter was reported to the throne, and he was told to proceed with the purchase.

sentences.zh: 已，奏闕里雅樂及樂舞生冠服敝壞，詔所司修治。

translations.literal: Later he memorialized that the court music at Que li and the caps and garments of the music and dance students were worn out; an edict ordered the responsible offices to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he reported that Qufu's court music and the caps and robes of the student musicians and dancers were in ruins; the responsible offices were ordered to restore them.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，帝幸學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai the emperor visited the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 the emperor visited the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 彥縉率三氏子孫觀禮，賜坐彜倫堂聽講。

translations.literal: Yanshen led descendants of the three clans to observe the rites and was granted a seat in the Hall of Human Relations to hear the lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen led descendants of the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans to witness the ceremony and was given a seat in the Hall of Human Relations to hear the lecture.

sentences.zh: 幸學必先期召衍聖公，自此始。

translations.literal: That the emperor, when visiting the academy, must beforehand summon the Duke of Yan Sheng began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward it became customary to summon the Duke of Yan Sheng in advance whenever the emperor visited the academy.

sentences.zh: 彥縉幼孤，能自立，然與族人不睦。

translations.literal: Yanshen was orphaned young but could stand on his own; yet he was not on good terms with his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yanshen nevertheless held his own, though he did not get on well with his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年，族祖克句等與彥縉相訐，帝置不問。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai, his clansmen Keju and others quarreled with Yanshen; the emperor set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 6 his kinsman Keju and others quarreled with Yanshen; the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 彥縉子承慶，先卒。

translations.literal: Yanshen's son Chengqing died first.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen's son Chengqing predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 孫弘緒，字以敬，甫八歲，而彥縉卒。

translations.literal: His grandson Hongxu, courtesy name Yijing, was only eight when Yanshen died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Hongxu, styled Yijing, was only eight when Yanshen died.

sentences.zh: 妾江訴弘緒幼弱，為族人所侵。

translations.literal: The concubine Jiang complained that Hongxu was young and weak and was being encroached upon by clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Jiang petitioned that Hongxu, still a child, was being bullied by kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 詔遣禮部郎為治喪，而命其族父公恂理家事。

translations.literal: An edict sent a secretary of the Ministry of Rites to manage the funeral, and ordered his clansman father Gongxun to handle family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched a secretary of the Ministry of Rites to oversee the funeral and charged his kinsman Gongxun with managing the household.

sentences.zh: 驛召弘緒至京襲封，賜玉帶金印，簡教授一人課其學。

translations.literal: By relay he was summoned to the capital to inherit the enfeoffment; a jade belt and gold seal were granted, and one instructor was selected to supervise his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu was summoned by relay to the capital to inherit the title, given a jade belt and gold seal, and assigned a tutor to oversee his education.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，入賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, he entered court to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong emperor was restored to the throne, Hongxu came to court to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 朝見便殿，握其手，置膝上，語良久。

translations.literal: He was received in audience at the informal hall; the emperor grasped his hand, set it on his knee, and spoke at length.
translations.idiomatic: Received in the informal hall, the emperor took his hand, rested it on his knee, and talked with him at length.

sentences.zh: 弘緒才十歲，進止有儀，帝甚悅。

translations.literal: Hongxu was only ten, yet in advancing and withdrawing he had proper bearing; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu was only ten, yet his bearing in court was impeccable, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 每歲入賀聖壽。

translations.literal: Each year he came to congratulate the emperor on his sacred birthday.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he came to court to offer birthday congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其賜第湫隘，以大第易之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the residence granted him was cramped and narrow, and exchanged it for a large mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his granted residence was cramped, the emperor exchanged it for a larger mansion.

sentences.zh: 凡南城賞花、西苑較射，皆與焉。

translations.literal: Whenever there was flower viewing in the southern city or archery contests in the Western Park, he took part in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was included in every southern-city flower viewing and Western Park archery contest.

sentences.zh: 公恂，字宗文。

translations.literal: Gongxun, courtesy name Zongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxun, whose courtesy name was Zongwen.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年舉會試。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 5 he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 聞母疾，不赴廷對。

translations.literal: Hearing that his mother was ill, he did not attend the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard his mother was ill, he did not go forward for the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 帝問禮部，得其故，遣使召之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the Ministry of Rites, learned the reason, and sent an envoy to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired at the Ministry of Rites, learned why, and sent an envoy to summon him.

sentences.zh: 日且午，不及備試卷，命翰林院給筆劄。

translations.literal: It was nearly noon and he had not time to prepare his examination papers; the Hanlin Academy was ordered to supply brush and paper.
translations.idiomatic: It was nearly noon and he had no time to prepare his papers; the Hanlin Academy was told to provide brush and stationery.

sentences.zh: 登第，即丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: He passed the grade and at once, on his mother's death, returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination and immediately went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 天順初，授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign he was made supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢言：「公恂，至聖後，贊善司馬恂，宋大賢溫國公光後，宜輔導太子。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian said: "Gongxun is a descendant of the Supreme Sage; Instructor Sima Xun is a descendant of the great Song worthy, Duke of Wen, Guang; they should guide the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Xian said: "Gongxun descends from the Supreme Sage; Instructor Sima Xun descends from the great Song worthy Sima Guang, Duke of Wen—they are fit to tutor the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 」帝喜，同日超拜少詹事，侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and on the same day promoted him to Junior Mentor, to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and that same day promoted him to Junior Mentor to lecture the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 入語孝肅皇后曰：「吾今日得聖賢子孫為汝子傅。

translations.literal: He went in and said to Empress Xiaosu: "Today I have obtained descendants of sages and worthies as tutors for your son."
translations.idiomatic: He went in and told Empress Xiaosu: "Today I have found descendants of sages to tutor your son."

sentences.zh: 」孝肅皇后者，憲宗生母，方以皇貴妃有寵，於是具冠服拜謝，宮中傳為盛事雲。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaosu was the birth mother of Emperor Xianzong and was then favored as Imperial Noble Consort; she thereupon put on full cap and robes and bowed in thanks—a matter the palace spread as a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaosu was the Xianzong emperor's birth mother and then held favor as Imperial Noble Consort; she donned full court dress and bowed in thanks, and the palace hailed it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 成化初，以言事謫漢陽知府，未至，丁父憂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, for remonstrance on affairs he was demoted to prefect of Hanyang; before he arrived, his father died and he entered mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was demoted to prefect of Hanyang for a memorial; before he took up the post his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，還故秩，蒞南京詹事府。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended he returned to his former rank and took up office at the Nanjing Mentorship Office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was restored to his former rank and took charge of the Nanjing Mentorship Office.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 弘緒少貴，又恃婦翁大學士李賢，多過舉。

translations.literal: Hongxu was exalted from youth and moreover relied on his father-in-law, Grand Secretary Li Xian, and often overstepped in his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Raised young to high rank and backed by his father-in-law Grand Secretary Li Xian, Hongxu often overreached.

sentences.zh: 成化五年被劾，按治，奪爵為庶人，令其弟弘泰襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua he was impeached, investigated, and stripped of his title to become a commoner; his younger brother Hongtai was ordered to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 5 he was impeached, investigated, and reduced to commoner status; his younger brother Hongtai was made to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 弘泰歿，爵仍歸弘緒子。

translations.literal: When Hongtai died, the title returned to Hongxu's son.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongtai died, the title reverted to Hongxu's line.

sentences.zh: 弘泰，字以和。

translations.literal: Hongtai, courtesy name Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtai, whose courtesy name was Yihe.

sentences.zh: 既嗣爵，弘治十一年，山東按臣言弘緒遷善改行，命復冠帶。

translations.literal: After he inherited the title, in the eleventh year of Hongzhi the Shandong surveillance commissioner reported that Hongxu had turned to goodness and reformed his conduct; he was ordered to restore cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: After succeeding to the title, in Hongzhi 11 the Shandong surveillance commissioner reported that Hongxu had mended his ways; he was allowed to resume cap and belt.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，聖殿災，弘泰方在朝，弘緒率子弟奔救，素服哭廟，蔬食百日。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year the Sage's hall caught fire; Hongtai was at court, while Hongxu led sons and younger kinsmen in a rush to save it, wore plain dress and wept at the temple, and ate only vegetables for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The following sixth month the Sage's hall burned; Hongtai was at court while Hongxu led the younger generation to the rescue, wore mourning dress and wept at the temple, and ate only plain food for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 弘泰還，亦齋哭如居喪。

translations.literal: When Hongtai returned, he likewise fasted and wept as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongtai returned, he too fasted and mourned as for a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 弘泰生七月而孤，奉母孝，與弘緒友愛，無間言。

translations.literal: Hongtai was orphaned at seven months, served his mother filially, and was friendly with Hongxu without a harsh word between them.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven months, Hongtai was filial to his mother and lived in harmony with Hongxu without a harsh word between them.

sentences.zh: 十六年卒，弘緒子聞韶襲。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died; Hongxu's son Wenshao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year; Hongxu's son Wenshao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 聞韶，字知德。

translations.literal: Wenshao, courtesy name Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao, whose courtesy name was Zhide.

sentences.zh: 明年，新廟建，規制逾舊，遣大學士李東陽祭告，禦制碑文勒石。

translations.literal: The next year the new temple was built, its regulations surpassing the old; Grand Secretary Li Dongyang was sent to announce the sacrifice, and an imperial inscription was carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a new temple was completed on a grander scale than before; Grand Secretary Li Dongyang was sent to announce the sacrifice, and the emperor's inscription was cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 正德三年以尼山、洙泗二書院及鄒縣子思子廟各有禮事，奏請弟聞禮主之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, because the Ni Mountain and Zhu-Si academies and the temple of Zisi at Zou County each had ritual duties, he memorialized that his younger brother Wenli should preside over them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 3, noting that the Ni Mountain and Zhu-Si academies and the Zisi temple at Zou County each required ritual oversight, he asked that his younger brother Wenli be put in charge.

sentences.zh: 帝授聞禮《五經》博士，主子思子祀事，世以衍聖公弟為之。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Wenli Doctor of the Five Classics, to preside over sacrifices to Zisi; thereafter the younger brother of the Duke of Yan Sheng held the post by hereditary custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wenli Doctor of the Five Classics to oversee sacrifices to Zisi; thereafter the duke's younger brother held the post by hereditary custom.

sentences.zh: 兩書院各設學錄一人，薦族之賢者充焉。

translations.literal: Each of the two academies was given one registrar, filled by recommending worthy men of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Each academy was given one registrar, drawn from worthy men of the clan.

sentences.zh: 六年，山東盜起，聞韶與巡撫趙璜請城闕里，遷曲阜縣治以衛廟，不果行。

translations.literal: In the sixth year bandits rose in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang requested walling Que li and moving the Qufu county seat to guard the temple—the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year bandits broke out in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang proposed fortifying Qufu and moving the county seat to protect the temple, but the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十五年，聞韶卒，子貞幹襲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing, Wenshao died; his son Zhengan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao died in Jiajing 25; his son Zhengan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 貞幹，字用濟。

translations.literal: Zhengan, courtesy name Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengan, whose courtesy name was Yongji.

sentences.zh: 三十五年入朝。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 卒，子尚賢襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Shangxian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Shangxian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尚賢，字象之。

translations.literal: Shangxian, courtesy name Xiangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxian, whose courtesy name was Xiangzhi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫丁以忠言：「尚賢沖年，宜如弘泰例，國學肄業。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ding Yizhong said: "Shangxian is young; following Hongtai's precedent, he should pursue studies at the Imperial Academy."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ding Yizhong said: "Shangxian is still young; following Hongtai's precedent, he should study at the Imperial Academy."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 萬歷九年，庶母郭氏訐尚賢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli his stepmother, the Guo clan, accused Shangxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 9 his stepmother of the Guo clan brought charges against Shangxian.

sentences.zh: 帝為革供奉女樂二十六戶，令三歲一朝。

translations.literal: The emperor abolished the twenty-six households of female musicians in his service and ordered court audiences once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed the twenty-six households of female musicians from his retinue and required him to come to court only once every three years.

sentences.zh: 十七年，尚賢仍請比歲入賀，許之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Shangxian again requested annual birthday congratulations at court; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Shangxian petitioned to resume annual birthday audiences; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尚賢博識。

translations.literal: Shangxian was broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxian was a man of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianqi 1.

sentences.zh: 子蔭椿先卒，無嗣，從弟子蔭植襲。

translations.literal: His son Yinchun died first without heirs; a younger clansman's son, Yinzhi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yinchun predeceased him without heirs, and a younger kinsman's son, Yinzhi, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 蔭植，字對寰。

translations.literal: Yinzhi, courtesy name Duihuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhi, whose courtesy name was Duihuan.

sentences.zh: 祖貞寧，衍聖公貞幹弟也，仕為《五經》博士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhenning was the younger brother of Duke Zhengan and served as Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhenning was the younger brother of Duke Zhengan and held the post of Doctor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 父尚坦，國學生，追封衍聖公。

translations.literal: His father Shangtan was a student of the Imperial Academy and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shangtan had been an Imperial Academy student and was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 蔭植先為博士，尚賢既喪子，遂育為嗣。

translations.literal: Yinzhi had first been a doctor; when Shangxian lost his son, he was raised as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhi had first served as Doctor of the Five Classics; after Shangxian lost his son, he was adopted as heir.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年以覃恩加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi, by grace of universal favor, he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 4 a general amnesty raised him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 彥繩卒，子承美，字永實，十四年襲。

translations.literal: When Yansheng died, his son Chengmei, courtesy name Yongshi, inherited in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: When Yansheng died, his son Chengmei, styled Yongshi, succeeded in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 卒，子弘章，字以達，嘉靖二十六年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Hongzhang, courtesy name Yida, inherited in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Hongzhang, styled Yida, succeeded in Jiajing 26.

sentences.zh: 卒，子聞音，字知政，萬歷五年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Wenyin, courtesy name Zhizheng, inherited in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Wenyin, styled Zhizheng, succeeded in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 卒，子貞運，字用行，四十三年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zhenyun, courtesy name Yongxing, inherited in the forty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Zhenyun, styled Yongxing, succeeded in the forty-third year.

sentences.zh: 時以在曲阜者為孔氏北宗，在西安者為南宗雲。

translations.literal: At that time those at Qufu were called the Northern lineage of the Kong clan, and those at Xi'an the Southern lineage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the line at Qufu was known as the Northern branch of the Kong clan, and that at Xi'an as the Southern branch.

sentences.zh: 顏希惠，復聖五十九代孫也。

translations.literal: Yan Xihui was a descendant of the Sage of Return in the fifty-ninth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xihui was a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of Yan Hui, the Sage of Return.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以顏子五十七代孫池為宣德府學教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, Chi, fifty-seventh-generation descendant of Yanzi, was made instructor at the Xuande Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign, Chi, fifty-seventh in descent from Yan Hui, was appointed instructor at the Xuande prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 十五年改三氏學教授，以奉祀事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was changed to instructor at the Three-Clan school, to perform sacrificial duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to professor at the Three-Clan school to oversee sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 池，字德裕。

translations.literal: Chi, courtesy name Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, whose courtesy name was Deyu.

sentences.zh: 子拳，字克膺。

translations.literal: His son Quan, courtesy name Keying.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan, styled Keying.

sentences.zh: 拳子希仁，字士元。

translations.literal: Quan's son Xiren, courtesy name Shiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's son Xiren, styled Shiyuan.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年詔以顏、孟子孫長而賢者各一人，至京官之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai an edict ordered that one eldest and worthy descendant each of Yan and Mencius come to the capital for office.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3 an edict called for one eldest worthy descendant each of the Yan and Meng lines to come to the capital for appointment.

sentences.zh: 其年，希仁為巡按御史顧躭所劾。

translations.literal: That year Xiren was impeached by touring censor Gu Dan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Xiren was impeached by touring censor Gu Dan.

sentences.zh: 詔黜希仁，召希惠以為翰林院《五經》博士。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Xiren and summoned Xihui to be Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Xiren and summoned Xihui to serve as Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以希惠非嫡子，仍以希仁長子議為之。

translations.literal: Before long, because Xihui was not the son of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because Xihui was not born of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was reappointed instead.

sentences.zh: 議，字定伯，成化元年賜第京師，入覲，馳驛以為常。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Dingbo, was granted a residence in the capital in the first year of Chenghua; when he came to audience, relay transport became his regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Dingbo, received a residence in the capital in Chenghua 1; on his court visits relay horses became routine.

sentences.zh: 議卒，子鋐，字宗器，十八年襲。

translations.literal: When Yi died, his son Hong, courtesy name Zongqi, inherited in the eighteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, his son Hong, styled Zongqi, succeeded in the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 卒，子重德，字尚本，正德二年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chongde, courtesy name Shangben, inherited in the second year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Chongde, styled Shangben, succeeded in Zhengde 2.

sentences.zh: 卒，子從祖，字守嗣，襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Congzu, courtesy name Shousi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Congzu, styled Shousi, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，嘉靖四十一年以從祖從父重禮之長子肇先為嗣。

translations.literal: He died without sons; in the forty-first year of Jiajing Congzu's father's younger brother Chongli's eldest son Zhaoxian was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons; in Jiajing 41 Chongli's eldest son Zhaoxian, a cousin of Congzu's generation, was made heir.

sentences.zh: 肇先，字啟源。

translations.literal: Zhaoxian, courtesy name Qiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxian, whose courtesy name was Qiyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，子嗣慎，字用修襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Sizhen, courtesy name Yongxiu, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Sizhen, styled Yongxiu, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，長子尹宗先卒，次子尹祚，字永錫，萬歷年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his eldest son Yinzong died first; his second son Yinhuo, courtesy name Yongxi, inherited in the Wanli years.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his eldest son Yinzong predeceased him; his second son Yinhuo, styled Yongxi, succeeded in the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 尹祚為人博學好義，尹宗之子伯貞既長，遂以其職讓之。

translations.literal: Yinhuo was by nature broadly learned and fond of righteousness; when Yinzong's son Bozhen had grown up, he yielded the post to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yinhuo was learned and public-spirited; when Yinzong's son Bozhen came of age, he yielded the post to him.

sentences.zh: 伯貞，字叔節，二十七年襲。

translations.literal: Bozhen, courtesy name Shujie, inherited in the twenty-seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen, styled Shujie, succeeded in the twenty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 卒，子幼，弟伯廉，字叔清，三十四年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son was young; his younger brother Bolian, courtesy name Shuqing, inherited in the thirty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving a young son; his younger brother Bolian, styled Shuqing, succeeded in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 卒，子紹緒，崇禎十四年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Shaoxu inherited in the fourteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Shaoxu succeeded in Chongzhen 14.

sentences.zh: 曾質粹，字好古，吉安永豐人，宗聖五十九代孫也。

translations.literal: Zeng Zhicui, courtesy name Haogu, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an and a descendant of the Sage of the Zeng clan in the fifty-ninth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Zhicui, styled Haogu, was from Yongfeng in Ji'an and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of Zengzi, the Sage of the Zeng clan.

sentences.zh: 其先，都鄉侯據避新莽之亂，徙家豫章，子孫散居撫、吉諸郡間。

translations.literal: His ancestor, Marquis of Duxiang Ju, fleeing the disorder of Xin Mang, moved his household to Yuzhang; descendants scattered among the prefectures of Fu and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor, Marquis Ju of Duxiang, fled the Xin Mang turmoil and settled in Yuzhang; later generations spread across Fu and Ji prefectures.

sentences.zh: 成化初，山東守臣上言：「嘉祥縣南武山西南，元寨山之東麓，有漁者陷入穴中，得懸棺，碣曰曾參之墓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua the Shandong guardian officials memorialized: "Southwest of Mount Nanwu in Jiaxiang County, on the eastern slope of Mount Yuanzhai, a fisherman fell into a cave and found a suspended coffin; a stele read 'Tomb of Zeng Shen.'"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign Shandong officials reported: "Southwest of Mount Nanwu in Jiaxiang County, on the eastern slope of Mount Yuanzhai, a fisherman fell into a cave and found a suspended coffin; the stele read 'Tomb of Zeng Shen.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔加修築。

translations.literal: An edict ordered additional repair and construction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the site restored and enlarged.

sentences.zh: 正德間，山東僉事錢鋐訪得曾子之後一人於嘉祥山中，未幾而沒。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, Shandong Vice Commissioner Qian Hong found one descendant of Zengzi in the Jiaxiang hills; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign Shandong Vice Commissioner Qian Hong found a descendant of Zengzi in the Jiaxiang hills, but he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十二年，以學士顧鼎臣言，詔求嫡嗣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiajing, on the word of Academician Gu Dingchen, an edict sought the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 12, on Academician Gu Dingchen's recommendation, an edict was issued to seek the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 於是江西撫按以質粹名聞，命回嘉祥，以衣巾奉祀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Jiangxi grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner reported Zhicui's name; he was ordered to return to Jiaxiang and perform sacrifices in ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi authorities then nominated Zhicui; he was ordered back to Jiaxiang to perform sacrifices in scholar's dress.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a post made hereditary for his line.

sentences.zh: 三十九年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 子昊，未襲卒。

translations.literal: His son Hao died before inheriting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao died before succeeding to the post.

sentences.zh: 昊子繼祖，字繩之，少病目，江西族人袞謀奪其職，為給事中劉不息、御史劉光國所糾，於是罷袞官，而繼祖仍主祀事。

translations.literal: Hao's son Jizu, courtesy name Shengzhi, had eye trouble from youth; a Jiangxi clansman Gun plotted to seize his office and was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was dismissed from office, and Jizu still presided over sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's son Jizu, styled Shengzhi, had been partly blind from youth; a Jiangxi kinsman named Gun tried to seize the post but was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was removed from office and Jizu retained charge of the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卒，子承業，字洪福，萬歷五年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chengye, courtesy name Hongfu, inherited in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Chengye, styled Hongfu, succeeded in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 卒，子弘毅，字泰東，崇禎元年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Hongyi, courtesy name Taidong, inherited in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Hongyi, styled Taidong, succeeded in Chongzhen 1.

sentences.zh: 卒，子聞達，字象輿，十四年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Wenda, courtesy name Xiangyu, inherited in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Wenda, styled Xiangyu, succeeded in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 孔聞禮，字知節，衍聖公聞韶弟也。

translations.literal: Kong Wenli, courtesy name Zhijie, was the younger brother of Duke Wenshao.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenli, styled Zhijie, was the younger brother of Duke Wenshao.

sentences.zh: 正德二年詔授翰林院《五經》博士，以奉述聖祀事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde an edict appointed him Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy to perform sacrifices to the Sage of Narration.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2 an edict made him Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics to oversee sacrifices to Zisi.

sentences.zh: 自後，世以衍聖公弟為之。

translations.literal: From then on, the younger brother of the Duke of Yan Sheng held the post by hereditary custom.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the duke's younger brother held the post by hereditary custom.

sentences.zh: 聞禮卒，嘉靖二十五年，貞寧字用致襲。

translations.literal: When Wenli died, in the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing Zhenning, courtesy name Yongzhi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenli died, Zhenning, styled Yongzhi, succeeded in Jiajing 25.

sentences.zh: 卒，萬歷二十二年，蔭桂襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the twenty-second year of Wanli Yingui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Yingui succeeded in Wanli 22.

sentences.zh: 卒，天啟二年，蔭隆襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the second year of Tianqi Yinlong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Yinlong succeeded in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 卒，八年，尚達襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the eighth year Shangda inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Shangda succeeded in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 卒，崇禎十年，蔭相襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the tenth year of Chongzhen Yinxiang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Yinxiang succeeded in Chongzhen 10.

sentences.zh: 卒，十四年，蔭錫襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the fourteenth year Yinxi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Yinxi succeeded in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 卒，十六年，蔭鈺襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the sixteenth year Yinyu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Yinyu succeeded in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 孟希文，字士煥，亞聖五十六代孫也。

translations.literal: Meng Xiwen, courtesy name Shihuan, was a descendant of the Second Sage in the fifty-sixth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xiwen, styled Shihuan, was a fifty-sixth-generation descendant of Mencius, the Second Sage.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年詔以孟子五十四代孫思諒奉祀，世復其家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu an edict ordered Siliao, fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Mencius, to perform sacrifices, and his household was restored by hereditary grant.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 an edict appointed Siliao, fifty-fourth in descent from Mencius, to perform sacrifices and restored his household by hereditary grant.

sentences.zh: 思諒，字友道，子克仁，字信夫。

translations.literal: Siliao, courtesy name Youdao; his son Keren, courtesy name Xinfu.
translations.idiomatic: Siliao, styled Youdao; his son Keren, styled Xinfu.

sentences.zh: 克仁子希文。

translations.literal: Keren's son was Xiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Keren's son was Xiwen.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年授希文翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai Xiwen was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3 Xiwen was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post for his line.

sentences.zh: 卒，子元，字長伯，弘治二年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yuan, courtesy name Changbo, inherited in the second year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Yuan, styled Changbo, succeeded in Hongzhi 2.

sentences.zh: 卒，子公棨幼，嘉靖二年以元弟亨之子公肇襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Gongqi was young; in the second year of Jiajing Yuan's younger brother Heng's son Gongzhao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving a young son Gongqi; in Jiajing 2 Yuan's nephew Gongzhao, son of his brother Heng, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 公肇，字先文，少好學，事繼母孔氏，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Gongzhao, courtesy name Xianwen, loved study from youth and served his stepmother of the Kong clan with filial conduct, for which he was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhao, styled Xianwen, was studious from youth and famed for filial service to his Kong-clan stepmother.

sentences.zh: 卒，十二年，仍以公棨襲。

translations.literal: He died; in the twelfth year Gongqi still inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; in the twelfth year the title passed back to Gongqi.

sentences.zh: 公棨，字橐文。

translations.literal: Gongqi, courtesy name Tuowen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongqi, whose courtesy name was Tuowen.

sentences.zh: 卒，子彥璞，字朝璽，隆慶元年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yanpu, courtesy name Chaoxi, inherited in the first year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Yanpu, styled Chaoxi, succeeded in Longqing 1.

sentences.zh: 卒，子承光，萬歷二十九年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chengguang inherited in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Chengguang succeeded in Wanli 29.

sentences.zh: 卒，子弘譽，天啟三年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Hongyu inherited in the third year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Hongyu succeeded in Tianqi 3.

sentences.zh: 卒，子聞玉，崇禎二年襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Wenyu inherited in the second year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Wenyu succeeded in Chongzhen 2.

sentences.zh: 仲於陛，先賢仲子六十二代孫也。

translations.literal: Zhong Yubi was a descendant of the former worthy Zhongzi in the sixty-second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yubi was a sixty-second-generation descendant of Zhongzi, the former worthy.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十五年詔以仲子五十九代孫呂為奉祀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Wanli an edict appointed Lü, fifty-ninth-generation descendant of Zhongzi, to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 15 an edict appointed Lü, fifty-ninth in descent from Zhongzi, to perform sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 呂子銓。

translations.literal: Lü Ziquan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ziquan.

sentences.zh: 銓子則顯。

translations.literal: Quan's son was Zexian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's son was Zexian.

sentences.zh: 則顯子於陛。

translations.literal: Zexian's son was Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Zexian's son was Yubi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年以衍聖公孔蔭植言，詔授於陛翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，賜泗水縣、濟寧州田六十余頃，廟戶三十一，以奉其祭祀焉。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, on the word of Duke of Yan Sheng Kong Yinzhi, an edict appointed Yubi Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, and granted more than sixty qing of fields in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture and thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 16, on Duke Yinzhi's recommendation, an edict made Yubi Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, and granted more than sixty qing of land in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture plus thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 周冕，先賢元公周子十二代孫也。

translations.literal: Zhou Mian was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Yuan, Master Zhou, in the twelfth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian was a twelfth-generation descendant of Zhou Dunyi, the former worthy Lord Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其先，道州人，熙寧中，周子葬母江州，子孫因家廬山蓮花峰下。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Daozhou; in the Xining era Master Zhou buried his mother in Jiangzhou, and descendants thereupon made their home below Lotus Peak on Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were from Daozhou; during the Xining reign Zhou Dunyi buried his mother in Jiangzhou, and his descendants settled below Lotus Peak on Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年，授冕翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，還鄉以奉周子祀事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai Mian was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, and returned home to perform sacrifices to Master Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 7 Mian was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post, and returned home to oversee sacrifices to Zhou Dunyi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子繡麟襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Xiulin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Xiulin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子道襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Dao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Dao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子聯芳襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Lianfang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Lianfang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子濟襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Ji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，從弟汝忠襲。

translations.literal: He died; his younger cousin Ruzhong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his younger cousin Ruzhong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子蓮應襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Lianying inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Lianying succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 程接道，先賢正公程子後也。

translations.literal: Cheng Jiedao was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Zheng, Master Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiedao was a descendant of Cheng Hao, the former worthy Lord Zheng.

sentences.zh: 宋淳熙間，純公程子五世孫有居江寧者，嘗主金陵書院祀事。

translations.literal: During the Chunxi years of Song, a fifth-generation descendant of Lord Chun, Master Cheng, who lived in Jiangning, once presided over sacrifices at the Jinling Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song Chunxi era a fifth-generation descendant of Cheng Yi who lived in Jiangning once oversaw sacrifices at the Jinling Academy.

sentences.zh: 卒，以名幼學者承之。

translations.literal: On his death a youth famed for learning succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, a promising young scholar succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 明初失傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming the line was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming the line was lost.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，河南巡按李日宣請以正公之後為之嗣，詔許之，遂以接道為翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen Henan touring censor Li Rixuan requested that a descendant of Lord Zheng succeed to the post; an edict granted this, and Jiedao was made Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 Henan touring censor Li Rixuan asked that a descendant of Cheng Hao be appointed; the throne agreed, and Jiedao was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line.

sentences.zh: 十四年，土賊於大忠作亂，接道力拒，死之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the bandit Yu Dazhong rebelled; Jiedao resisted with all his strength and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the bandit Yu Dazhong rose in revolt; Jiedao resisted fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 程克仁，先賢正公程子十七代孫也，世居嵩縣之六渾。

translations.literal: Cheng Keren was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Zheng, Master Cheng, in the seventeenth generation, his clan long dwelling at Liuhun in Song County.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Keren was a seventeenth-generation descendant of Cheng Hao and his family had long lived at Liuhun in Song County.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年授翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，以奉程子祀事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai he was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, to perform sacrifices to Master Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 6 he was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post charged with sacrifices to Cheng Hao.

sentences.zh: 卒，子繼祖襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jizu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Jizu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，仲子世宥襲。

translations.literal: He died; his second son Shiyou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his second son Shiyou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子心傳襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Xinchuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Xinchuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 心傳莊重寡言，為鄉黨所稱。

translations.literal: Xinchuan was grave and sparing of speech and was praised in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchuan was grave and sparing of speech and was well regarded in his community.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟宗益襲。

translations.literal: He died; his younger brother Zongyi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his younger brother Zongyi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，從子佳引襲。

translations.literal: He died; his nephew Jiayin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his nephew Jiayin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，從弟佳祚襲。

translations.literal: He died; his younger cousin Jiazuo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his younger cousin Jiazuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年為土賊於大忠所殺。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he was killed by the bandit Yu Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 14 he was killed by the bandit Yu Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 張文運，郿人，先賢明公張子十四代孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenyun, a native of Mei, was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Ming, Master Zhang, in the fourteenth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenyun, from Mei, was a fourteenth-generation descendant of Zhang Zai, the former worthy Lord Ming.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年授翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，以奉張子祀事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, to perform sacrifices to Master Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post charged with sacrifices to Zhang Zai.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年卒，子承引，以父憂未襲。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Chongzhen; his son Chengyin, because of mourning for his father, had not yet inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongzhen 3; his son Chengyin had not yet succeeded, being in mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，子元祥，本朝康熙元年襲。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year; his son Yuanxiang inherited in the first year of Kangxi of our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year; his son Yuanxiang succeeded in Kangxi 1 of the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 邵繼祖，洛陽人，先賢康節公邵子二十七代孫也。

translations.literal: Shao Jizu, a native of Luoyang, was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Kangjie, Master Shao, in the twenty-seventh generation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jizu, from Luoyang, was a twenty-seventh-generation descendant of Shao Yong, the former worthy Lord Kangjie.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，河南巡按吳甡請以繼祖為翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，以奉邵子祀事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen Henan touring censor Wu Shen requested that Jizu be made Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, to perform sacrifices to Master Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 Henan touring censor Wu Shen asked that Jizu be made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, to oversee sacrifices to Shao Yong.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 卒，子養醇襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yangchun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Yangchun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 朱梴，字孟齡，先賢文公朱子九世孫也，世居福建建安縣之紫霞洲。

translations.literal: Zhu Ting, courtesy name Mengling, was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Wen, Master Zhu, in the ninth generation, his clan long dwelling at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ting, styled Mengling, was a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi and his family had long lived at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年授翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲，以奉朱子祀事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai he was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants, to perform sacrifices to Master Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 6 he was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post charged with sacrifices to Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 梴為人淳謹，言動有則。

translations.literal: Ting was by nature simple and careful; in word and deed he had standards.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was plain and careful by nature, and measured in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 卒，子燉，字孔暉襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Dun, courtesy name Konghui, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Dun, styled Konghui, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 燉以事入都，中途遇盜。

translations.literal: Dun entered the capital on business and met bandits on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Dun traveled to the capital on business and was robbed on the road.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有遺金道上者，燉守之，以還其人，人稱其廉介。

translations.literal: Before long someone left gold on the road; Dun guarded it and returned it to the owner, and people praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward someone dropped gold on the road; Dun kept watch over it and returned it to the owner, and people praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 卒，子塋，字元厚襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Ying, courtesy name Yuanhou, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Ying, styled Yuanhou, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子鎏襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Liu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Liu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子法，字兆祖襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Fa, courtesy name Zhaozu, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Fa, styled Zhaozu, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 法為人孝友。

translations.literal: Fa was by nature filial and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Fa was known for filial piety and brotherly kindness.

sentences.zh: 卒，子楗，字士啟襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jian, courtesy name Shiqi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Jian, styled Shiqi, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子瑩，字惟玉襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Ying, courtesy name Weiyu, inherited.

sentences.zh: 朱墅，先賢文公朱子十一世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhu Shu was a descendant of the former worthy Lord Wen, Master Zhu, in the eleventh generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shu was an eleventh-generation descendant of Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 正德間，給事中戴銑、汪元錫，御史王完等相繼言：「朱子，繼孔子者也。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, supervising secretaries Dai Xian and Wang Yuanxi and censor Wang Wan and others said in succession: "Master Zhu succeeded Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign supervising secretaries Dai Xian and Wang Yuanxi, censor Wang Wan, and others said in turn: "Master Zhu stands in succession to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 孔子之後有曲阜、西安，朱子之後亦有建安、婺源。

translations.literal: After Confucius there are Qufu and Xi'an; after Master Zhu there are also Jian'an and Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius has descendants at Qufu and Xi'an; Zhu Xi has descendants at Jian'an and Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 今建安恩典已隆，在婺源者，請依闕里之例，錄其子孫一人，量授以官，俾掌祠事。

translations.literal: Now favors to Jian'an are already generous; for those at Wuyuan, we beg that following the precedent of Que li one descendant be recorded and granted office in due measure, to preside over temple affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Favors to Jian'an are already ample; for Wuyuan we ask that, following the Qufu precedent, one descendant be registered and given a modest office to oversee the temple."

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年授墅翰林院《五經》博士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing Shu was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 Shu was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 三十八年以本學訓導席端言，令其世襲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, on the word of the instructor of the local school, Xi Duan, he was ordered to hold the post by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, on the recommendation of local school instructor Xi Duan, the post was made hereditary.
